## README.md
# SNOTEL and SCAN station archive (USDA NRCS)

The USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service's automated snow and soil station
networks (SNOTEL snow telemetry, its SNOWLITE satellites, and SCAN soil climate)
as a self-contained cloud-native archive: the complete daily observational record with
NRCS's quality-control history on every row, the station map, the sensor inventory, and
the 30-year normals. Everything needed to use these networks without touching an API.

145 million daily values across 1,219 telemetry stations, 184 MB total. Thirteen
elements: WTEQ (snow water equivalent, inches), SNWD (snow depth), SNDN (snow density,
pct), SNRR (snow/rain ratio), PREC (accumulated precipitation), PRCP (daily
precipitation increment), PRCPSA (snow-adjusted increment), TOBS / TMAX / TMIN / TAVG
(air temperature, °F), and, at every installed sensor depth, SMS (soil moisture, pct)
and STO (soil temperature, °F). Values as served by the AWDB REST API v1; no resampling,
no gap filling. Where NRCS revised a reading during quality control, both the
current and the original value are here.

## Layout

```
stations.parquet           3,929 stations (includes 2,708 manual snow courses whose
                           semi-monthly history is coming in a follow-up pass).
                           GeoParquet 1.1: WKB points, covering bbox column,
                           dataset extent, OGC:CRS84.
station_elements.parquet   the sensor inventory: one row per (station, element,
                           duration, depth, ordinal) with its period of record,
                           i.e. what each station can answer, and since when.
latest.parquet             the newest reading of every live series (48 KB): one row
                           per (station, element, depth), with a datetime and a
                           duration column. The fast lane for any "current
                           conditions" map. Today it is fed from the daily record;
                           the planned refresh feeds it from hourly telemetry
                           (same schema, fresher rows).
normals/daily_normals.parquet   30-year (1991-2020) day-of-year median and average
                           (WTEQ, SNWD, PREC) for the 781 stations NRCS computes
                           them for.
normals/swe_timing.parquet median snowpack peak / onset / melt-out date and SWE
                           per station.
daily/archive.parquet      the daily record through the last completed water year
                           (Sep 30). Rewritten only quarterly, when a full re-crawl
                           picks up older revisions.
daily/current.parquet      the current water year; the daily refresh rewrites this
                           small file.
```

Both daily files share one long schema: station_triplet, network, state, element,
depth_in (int16, inches below surface, negative; NULL for non-soil elements),
date (date32), value (float32), qc_flag, qa_flag, orig_value, orig_qc_flag
(orig_* non-NULL means NRCS revised this reading; NULL means never revised).
Sorted (element, depth, station, date), zstd, 200k row groups. For any query,
read the pair: `read_parquet(['daily/archive.parquet', 'daily/current.parquet'])`.
Every file has a fixed name and URL; there is nothing to list or glob.

## Example queries (DuckDB, tested against this tree)

One station, any window, full history (the archive/current pair reads as one table):

```sql
SELECT date, value AS swe_in
FROM read_parquet(['daily/archive.parquet', 'daily/current.parquet'])
WHERE station_triplet = '766:UT:SNTL' AND element = 'WTEQ'
  AND date BETWEEN DATE '2026-05-15' AND DATE '2026-05-25' ORDER BY date;
-- Snowbird's 2026 melt-out: SWE hits zero on May 22.
```

Current conditions, every station, one 48 KB read:

```sql
SELECT station_triplet, state, datetime, value AS swe_in
FROM read_parquet('latest.parquet')
WHERE element = 'WTEQ' AND network = 'SNTL' ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 10;
```

The whole network (network and state are ordinary columns):

```sql
SELECT state, round(avg(value), 1) AS mean_april_swe_in
FROM read_parquet(['daily/archive.parquet', 'daily/current.parquet'])
WHERE network = 'SNTL' AND element = 'WTEQ' AND month(date) = 4
GROUP BY state ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```

The quality-control history: what did NRCS revise, and from what?

```sql
SELECT station_triplet, date, orig_value, orig_qc_flag, value, qc_flag
FROM read_parquet(['daily/archive.parquet', 'daily/current.parquet'])
WHERE element = 'WTEQ' AND orig_value IS NOT NULL AND abs(orig_value - value) > 5
ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 5;
-- e.g. a failed sensor reporting 72" of SWE in August, flagged S(uspect),
-- corrected to 0.0 E(dited). 43% of WTEQ rows carry a revision; 0.5% of TOBS.
```

Soil moisture with the station map: the latest 2-inch reading at every Alabama SCAN station.

```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
SELECT s.name, round(st_x(s.geometry), 3) AS lon, round(st_y(s.geometry), 3) AS lat,
       a.datetime, a.value AS sms_pct
FROM read_parquet('latest.parquet') a
JOIN read_parquet('stations.parquet') s USING (station_triplet)
WHERE a.element = 'SMS' AND a.depth_in = -2 AND a.network = 'SCAN' AND a.state = 'AL'
ORDER BY 1;
```

Percent of normal, the axis every SNOTEL plot uses:

```sql
SELECT d.date, d.value AS swe_in, n.median AS median_swe_in,
       round(100 * d.value / nullif(n.median, 0)) AS pct_of_median
FROM read_parquet(['daily/archive.parquet', 'daily/current.parquet']) d
JOIN read_parquet('normals/daily_normals.parquet') n
  ON n.station_triplet = d.station_triplet AND n.element = d.element
 AND n.month = month(d.date) AND n.day = day(d.date)
WHERE d.station_triplet = '766:UT:SNTL' AND d.element = 'WTEQ'
  AND d.date >= DATE '2026-04-01' ORDER BY d.date LIMIT 10;
```

Spatial join, stations near a point (the geometry column loads as a typed
GEOMETRY('OGC:CRS84') in DuckDB spatial; geopandas.read_parquet works unchanged):

```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
WITH near AS (
  SELECT station_triplet, name,
         ST_Distance_Sphere(geometry, ST_Point(-111.638, 40.591)) / 1000 AS km
  FROM read_parquet('stations.parquet')
  WHERE ST_Distance_Sphere(geometry, ST_Point(-111.638, 40.591)) < 15000)
SELECT n.name, round(n.km, 1) AS km, max(d.value) AS peak_swe_in
FROM near n
JOIN read_parquet(['daily/archive.parquet', 'daily/current.parquet']) d USING (station_triplet)
WHERE d.element = 'WTEQ' AND d.date >= DATE '2025-10-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY km;
```

## Reading without DuckDB

pyarrow prunes and pushes filters down over HTTP (a station query moves a few hundred
KB, not the file):

```python
import fsspec, pyarrow.dataset as ds, pyarrow.compute as pc
base = "https://data.source.coop/nthh/snotel/"
d = ds.dataset(base + "daily/archive.parquet", filesystem=fsspec.filesystem("https"))
df = d.to_table(columns=["date", "value"],
    filter=(pc.field("station_triplet") == "766:UT:SNTL") &
           (pc.field("element") == "WTEQ")).to_pandas()
```

```python
import fsspec, geopandas as gpd
with fsspec.open(base + "stations.parquet") as f:
    stations = gpd.read_parquet(f)   # typed geometry, OGC:CRS84
```

Two stdlib traps to avoid: `pd.read_parquet(url)` and bare `urllib` fail with 403
(the CDN rejects the `Python-urllib` user agent on full-object requests; ranged
requests and fsspec/aiohttp are fine), and `gpd.read_parquet(url)` does not accept
https URLs directly (wrap with `fsspec.open` as above).

## Provenance and license

Fetched from the AWDB REST API v1 (`wcc.sc.egov.usda.gov/awdbRestApi`), full period of
record through 2026-09-01, crawled 2026-09-01/02 (all 1,219 stations, zero skips).
Upstream data is a US Government work (public domain); this compilation is released
under CC0. The first consumer was a Sentinel-2 melt-out climatology validated against
Atwater and Snowbird, whose predicted June melt-out matches both the daily record here
and the medianMeltout normal (June 14 at Snowbird).

Prior art, gratefully: egagli/snotel_ccss_stations (daily CSVs on GitHub) and
scottyhq/snotel (the 2022 station-metadata groundwork).

## Design notes (why it is the way it is)

- **Why daily leads, and hourly is absent (for now).** The daily values are NRCS's
  edited, quality-controlled tier and run the full period of record (1978 onward);
  hourly is raw telemetry, dense only since ~2005, with sensor spikes and no editing.
  Nearly all snow science (melt-out dates, SWE peaks, climatology) runs on daily. An
  `hourly/` tree with the same archive/current shape will be added if there is demand.
- **Why archive + current instead of one file or append-only.** NRCS revises past
  values during quality control, so an append-only mirror would slowly diverge from
  the source of truth. Splitting at the water-year boundary means the daily refresh
  rewrites only the small current file, while a quarterly full re-crawl refreshes the
  frozen history to pick up older revisions.
- **Why a few single files instead of a partitioned tree.** At this size (184 MB),
  partitioning adds cost without benefit: the CDN serves files, not directory
  listings, so many files means hand-enumerated URLs, while row-group statistics on
  the sorted single file already prune any station/element/date query to one or two
  small range reads. Partitioning earns its keep at gigabytes; sorting does the work
  at megabytes. The global sort also compresses 2.4x better than the same rows split
  into 64 files.
- **Why fixed names.** Every file here has a stable, meaningful URL (no `part-0000`
  style names, which exist for listing-based readers). Queries and notebooks can
  hardcode paths and survive every refresh.
- **Why long format.** Elements start in different decades and soil sensors sit at
  25 distinct depths; as columns this would be a ragged, ever-migrating schema. As
  rows, adding an element is just more rows.
- **Why latest.parquet exists.** Date statistics cannot prune row groups that each
  span decades, so "every station right now" would otherwise scan the whole element
  section. One small file answers it in a single read, and its schema (datetime +
  duration) is ready to be fed from hourly telemetry without breaking consumers.

## Caveats

- The 2,708 manual snow-course stations (network SNOW) have no daily telemetry; their
  semi-monthly historical record (1930s onward) lands in a follow-up pass.
- `qc_flag` / `qa_flag` are NRCS's codes as served (V valid, E edited, S suspect,
  C composite, K estimated, ...). SNDN and SNRR are derived products and carry no
  revisions by construction.
- Soil depths follow each site's installation: -2 / -8 / -20 inches carry most of the
  record, with a long tail of site-specific depths (25 distinct values down to -80).
  Where a station has more than one sensor at the same depth, AWDB's default (ordinal 1)
  is what's here.
- Normals cover the 781 stations with a sufficient 1991-2020 record; newer stations have
  none. Leap day is absent from the day-of-year table.
- `end_date` of 2100-01-01 in the station table means "active".
- Units are AWDB-native (inches, °F, percent).

## Refresh

A daily job is planned; until it lands, treat this as a point-in-time snapshot dated in
the repo description. The refresh design: each day, refetch a trailing window (90 days),
merge last-write-wins, and rewrite `daily/current.parquet` and `latest.parquet` (a few
MB). Because NRCS revises past values during quality control (43% of all SWE rows have
been revised at least once), a quarterly full re-crawl rewrites `daily/archive.parquet`
to catch revisions older than the window. Files are replaced whole, never patched, and
never renamed. An `hourly/` tree with the same archive/current pair may follow if there
is demand.
